source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 9 mathematics textbooks

stages.headline: A side squared equals the sum of the squares of the other two minus twice their product times the cosine of the angle between them.
stages.headlineEnglish: A side squared equals the sum of the squares of the other two minus twice their product times the cosine of the angle between them.

stages.headline: If C = 90°, cos C = 0 and we get Pythagoras. Example: a = 3, b = 5, C = 120° ⇒ c² = 9 + 25 + 15 = 49, c = 7.
stages.headlineEnglish: If C = 90°, cos C = 0 and we get Pythagoras. Example: a = 3, b = 5, C = 120° ⇒ c² = 9 + 25 + 15 = 49, c = 7.

stages.headline: The law also gives angles: cos C = (a² + b² − c²) / 2ab; if c² > a² + b², C is obtuse.
stages.headlineEnglish: The law also gives angles: cos C = (a² + b² − c²) / 2ab; if c² > a² + b², C is obtuse.
